name: Pakistan

chips.label: Granted prosperity
chips.why: Wealth has outrun institutions - historically fragile.
chips.rule: MI residual vs. the log-GDP regression (the durability gap): below -0.03 → granted, otherwise earned (a ±0.03 tolerance treats near-zero gaps as in-line).

chips.label: Some imbalance · weakest: Stability & Resilience
chips.why: Spread between the strongest and weakest pillar - the country's structural shape.

verdict: Mixed structural profile - prosperity outrunning institutions.

checks.title: Durability gate
checks.headline: earned-vs-granted -0.09
checks.detail: This country's prosperity has outrun its institutions. Income the institutions cannot anchor is the classic fragility signal - historically it tends not to last.

checks.title: Weakest link
checks.headline: Stability & Resilience is lowest
checks.detail: Stability & Resilience is the pillar dragging the score down. A chain breaks at its weakest link, so this is where the structural risk concentrates.

checks.title: Room to rise
checks.headline: low base
checks.detail: Starting from a low institutional base, the country is structurally eligible to climb. This is eligibility, not a forecast - the effect only showed up strongly in the 2000s global growth wave.
